title: Can Language Models Build Molecules in Three Dimensions?
abstract:
arXiv:2611.25041v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Chemical drawings convey which atoms are bonded and how stereocentres are configured, but not molecular shape. Every simulation starts from three-dimensional coordinates, and building them from a drawing remains a manual step. We introduce MolDraft, a curated benchmark of 300 drawing-structure pairs spanning natural products, hypervalent compounds, and coordination complexes. Given an image and a short instruction, an AI system must generate a complete set of atomic coordinates, which are checked for molecular identity, stereochemical configuration, and coarse ligand geometry. We evaluate nine multimodal language models using the same agent setup. The share of molecules built correctly, the resolve rate, ranges from 25.0% to 76.0% and falls as molecules grow, most sharply above about 80 atoms. Only 29 of the 300 molecules are resolved by all nine models, and literature structures, mostly metal complexes, are the hardest source for every model. Language models can thus build many molecules in three dimensions, but not yet reliably reproduce the coordination chemistry of the research literature.
relevance_reason: Key author: Al\'an Aspuru-Guzik

title: MAPPA: Mapping of Atoms by Progressive Pattern Assembly with Molecular Symmetry
abstract:
arXiv:2611.25052v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Atom-to-atom mapping traces atom identities between molecular endpoints, supporting reaction anal- ysis and pathway construction. Yet the same endpoints can admit multiple correspondences, and selecting a single answer can conceal alternatives with different chemical implications. We introduce MAPPA, a framework that efficiently discovers and retains alternative atom mappings. It uses shared molecular fragments and molecular symmetry to represent these alternatives compactly, allowing their bond changes to be examined and supporting subsequent chemistry-aware selection. MAPPA achieves the highest reference coverage among the evaluated methods on Golden. Standard benchmark runs re- cover 99.03% of Golden and 99.63% of EnzymeMap reference mappings, with matching and decoding together averaging 3.19 and 13.16 CPU seconds per reaction, respectively. Broader exploration raises Golden coverage to 99.51%. These results make broad exploration of mapping alternatives practical, providing a foundation for studying reaction ambiguity and incorporating chemical knowledge into mapping selection.
relevance_reason: Key author: Alan Aspuru-Guzik

title: OpenTME: An Open Dataset of AI-powered H&E Tumor Microenvironment Profiles from TCGA
abstract:
arXiv:2604.12075v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: The tumor microenvironment (TME) plays a central role in cancer progression, treatment response, and patient outcomes, yet large-scale, consistent, and quantitative TME characterization from routine hematoxylin and eosin (H&E)-stained histopathology remains scarce. We introduce OpenTME, an open-access dataset of pre-computed TME profiles derived from 5,268 H&E-stained whole-slide images across ten cancer types (bladder, breast, colorectal, head and neck, liver, lung, ovarian, pancreatic, prostate, and stomach cancer) from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA). All outputs were generated using HETA (H&E Tissue Analysis), an AI-powered application built on the Atlas family of pathology foundation models, which performs tissue quality control, tissue segmentation, cell detection and classification, tumor zone and tertiary lymphoid structure (TLS) detection, and spatial neighborhood analysis, yielding over 20,000 quantitative readouts per slide at cell-level resolution, including curated features such as tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes, tumor mitotic index, or mature TLS counts. OpenTME is available for non-commercial academic research on Hugging Face. We will continue to expand OpenTME over time and anticipate it will serve as a resource for biomarker discovery, spatial biology research, and the development of computational methods for TME analysis.
relevance_reason: Key author: Klaus-Robert M\"uller

title: Emergent Fatigue Dynamics from Foundational Interatomic Potentials
abstract:
arXiv:2611.26533v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Foundational machine-learned interatomic potentials are trained on large, diverse DFT datasets, but their validation rests on equilibrium states, which does not guarantee correct emergent behavior in large-scale molecular dynamics. Where no direct experimental validation is available, comparisons to physically motivated potentials are valuable for drawing insight. We distinguish static properties, which are thermally accessible, from emergent properties, which require work from an external fatigue stress to drive rare events, and compare the potentials on both. An EAM potential and the NequIP foundational potential both agree closely with reference data for many near-equilibrium properties, but NequIP predicts an anomalously low intrinsic stacking fault energy ($\sim7$ times lower than EAM) and thus predicts far more plastic deformation under fatigue cycling of a nanoscale flaw modeled after the classical Griffith crack problem. Per-atom energy distributions after loading show that the two potentials differ most at energies far above what is thermally accessible. We also document memory-related crashes and silent extrapolation as practical concerns for practitioners of these foundational model forms.
relevance_reason: Benchmarks foundational MLIPs against EAM with large-scale MD fatigue simulations on explicit atomistic systems; directly satisfies (a)-(c).

title: Alloying effects on the interface cohesion of grain boundaries in the Ni--Fe--Cr system
abstract:
arXiv:2611.25944v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Grain boundaries (GBs) in polycrystalline Ni-based alloys strongly influence mechanical strength and fracture behavior, yet the effect of alloying elements such as Fe and Cr on GB cohesion remains difficult to quantify systematically. Using density functional theory (DFT), we compute rigid-body separation (RBS) curves for six symmetric-tilt Ni GBs, extracting the work of separation $W_{\mathrm{sep}}$ and maximum traction $\sigma_{\max}$ via the universal binding energy relation (UBER). We find that substitution of Cr or Fe into the GB plane increases both quantities relative to pure Ni GBs. To overcome the size limitations of DFT, we compare several machine-learning interatomic potential (MLIP) foundation models against the DFT dataset and identify a model achieving quantitative agreement with DFT for $W_{\mathrm{sep}}$ and $\sigma_{\max}$. This MLIP enables systematic sampling of alloying configurations at finer concentration steps. We show that alloying-induced changes in GB cohesion depend on both, element type and local structures, revealing trends that are inaccessible with DFT alone. Extending the analysis to a ternary $\mathrm{Ni}_{56}\mathrm{Fe}_{20}\mathrm{Cr}_{24}$ composition, inspired by the principal constituents of the widely used commercial Alloy 718, shows that the binary trends provide a useful basis for interpreting the combined effect of both substitutes, while explicit ternary calculations are required to capture their interplay quantitatively. Together, these results provide a validated workflow for quantifying the effect of alloying elements on GB cohesion in multicomponent alloys. The resulting values may serve as input for continuum-scale fracture models, paving the way toward atomistically informed multiscale modeling.
relevance_reason: DFT rigid-body separation calculations and MLIP benchmarking/application for Ni-Fe-Cr grain boundaries; explicitly atomistic and satisfies (a)-(c).

title: The phase diagram of fluid hydrogen near melting from machine-learned interatomic potentials trained on quantum Monte Carlo
abstract:
arXiv:2611.25178v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Dissociation of molecular hydrogen increasing temperature or pressure may either occur gradually or abruptly, via a phase transition. Despite considerable experimental and theoretical efforts, the phase diagram of dense hydrogen at temperatures above solid melting is not precisely known. Here, we perform classical and quantum Path Integral molecular dynamics simulations of dense hydrogen using two machine-learned interatomic potentials both trained on quantum Monte Carlo energies and forces. The resulting phase diagram is constructed using state-of-the-art techniques. Both models show a first-order phase transition from the molecular to the atomic liquid terminating in critical points whose locations were determined using finite-size scaling techniques. Triple points, located at the highest temperature of the melting curve, are found at the intersection of the liquid-liquid lines with the melting curve and should lead to clear signatures in ramp compression experiments.
relevance_reason: Trains machine-learned interatomic potentials on quantum Monte Carlo energies/forces and runs classical and path-integral MD to map the dense hydrogen phase diagram, clearly satisfying (a) explicit atoms, (b) MLIP development plus MD, and (c) application to a real material system.

title: Assessing the Transferability of General-Purpose MachineLearning Interatomic Potentials for Heterogeneous Catalysis with HetCat26
abstract:
arXiv:2609.30621v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Foundation machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) promise near-density functional theory (DFT) accuracy across broad areas of chemistry and materials science. However, their performance in describing systems and processes relevant to heterogeneous catalysis remains underexplored. Here, we introduce HetCat26, a collection of benchmark tests designed to assess pre-trained MLIPs across key aspects of catalytic modeling, including surface energetics, metal-metal oxide interactions, adsorption, and catalytic reaction networks. Evaluating eighteen foundation models, we find that performance on existing general materials benchmarks is only weakly predictive of performance on HetCat26; transferability to heterogeneous catalysis cannot be inferred from these general benchmarks. Across the benchmark tests, current models describe surface energetics and, perhaps surprisingly, reaction barriers well, whereas larger errors are observed for adsorption, and DFT site preferences are often not reproduced. Three models, eSEN-30M-OAM, SevenNet-Omni-i12 and MACE-MH-1-OMAT, nevertheless achieve high accuracy across the properties evaluated. Beyond model benchmarking, HetCat26 highlights the importance of training data consistency: PBE and PBE+U calculations should not be mixed within a training set. Overall, we identify challenges limiting the transferability of current foundation MLIPs to heterogeneous catalysis and, more broadly, to chemical reactions at interfaces, providing guidance for the development of the next generation of foundation models.
relevance_reason: A systematic benchmark of eighteen foundation MLIPs on catalytic surface, adsorption, and reaction-barrier tasks is squarely MLIP benchmarking on explicit atomistic systems, satisfying (a)-(c).

title: Machine Learning-Driven High-Throughput Screening of Equimolar and Non-Equimolar High-Entropy Carbides
abstract:
arXiv:2611.25127v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Search for optimal compositions among high-entropy ceramics are challenging due to large composition space, which are unable to test either experimentally or by \textit{ab initio} calculations. Here we present a high-throughput screening for equimolar and non-equimolar high-entropy carbides (HEC) among group IVB and VB transition metals (Ti, Zr, Hf, V, Nb and Ta). Large Atomistic Model MACE, and deep learning based interatomic potential DeePMD trained on \textit{ab initio}-based dataset of structures are used to effectively screen over the thousands of potential non-equimolar compositions among high-entropy carbides of Ti, Zr, Hf, V, Nb and Ta transition metals. A set of both equimolar and non-equimolar HECs are predicted to be stable in order to further synthesize those compositions based on the predictions.
relevance_reason: Uses MACE and DeePMD machine-learned interatomic potentials trained on ab initio data to screen high-entropy carbides; (a) explicit atoms, (b) MLIP training/application, (c) applied to stability screening.

title: A Liquid Film Can Survive without Being Bulk-Like: Rupture and Mechanical Isotropy Set Different Thickness Limits in Lennard-Jones Films
abstract:
arXiv:2611.25008v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: How thick must a liquid film be before its middle behaves like ordinary bulk liquid? Free-standing films are the standard geometry for computing surface properties by molecular simulation and the simplest model of soap and foam films, coatings and polymer layers, yet the question is seldom answered quantitatively. We answer it for Lennard-Jones films by comparing two criteria: whether the film survives without rupturing, and whether the lateral pressure at its center has relaxed to the bulk value. Covering three interaction ranges (cutoffs rc = 3.5-7.5 times sigma), three temperatures and lateral system sizes from 20 to 100 times sigma, we find that the two criteria give different thicknesses and respond to different parameters. Films thinner than 6-7 times sigma (about 2 nm for argon) rupture within 105 tau (~0.2 microseconds); this kinetic limit hardly depends on the interaction range but grows with the lateral size of the system, and close to it rupture is an activated event. The center becomes mechanically bulk-like only at a larger thickness h*, where the tangential anisotropy computed with the Irving-Kirkwood definition falls below 0.003 epsilon x sigma^3; h* grows from ~11 times sigma (3.8 nm) to ~15 times sigma (5 nm) as the cutoff increases from 3.5 to 7.5 times sigma, but it is nearly independent of temperature and of lateral size. Between the two limits films are long-lived yet perturbed throughout. Neither the surface tension, which shows no thickness dependence, nor the central density, whose relative deficit is about 16 times smaller than the relative anisotropy, reveals this perturbation: the stress detects confinement before the structure does.
relevance_reason: Classical molecular-dynamics simulations of free-standing Lennard-Jones films with Irving-Kirkwood pressure profiles to determine rupture and mechanical-bulk-like thickness limits: explicit atoms (a), MD with a classical force field (b), and a genuine physical result about thin-film behavior (c) are all satisfied.

title: AdsNet: A Graph Neural Network for Direct Adsorption Energy Prediction
abstract:
arXiv:2611.25646v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Fast and accurate prediction of adsorption energies is critical for high-throughput computational catalyst screening, existing methods compromise either on evaluation speed (full-graph machine learning potentials) or geometric sensitivity (coordination-based models like the alpha-scheme). Here, we present AdsNet, an equivariant graph neural network that directly predicts adsorption energies in a single forward pass, which operates on a local graph restricted only to adsorbate atoms and its immediate surface neighbors within a cutoff radius. This local graph formulation decouples computational complexity from total system size while encoding continuous geometric features (interatomic distances and directional vectors) enabling sensitivity to subtle variations in local bonding environments. AdsNet adopts a message-passing architecture with scalar and vector node features over multiple interaction layers. Trained on AdsTraj, a dataset of 33,920 density functional theory (DFT) calculated structures spanning 26 transition metals and 6 adsorbates (H*, C*, O*, CO*, OH*, HOCO*), the model achieves an adsorption energy root-mean-square error (RMSE) of 0.032 eV and a force RMSE of 0.047 eV/A. Analytic forces obtained via automatic differentiation enable structure relaxation through a projected gradient descent algorithm with adaptive line search, eliminating entire geometry optimizations. Additionally, AdsNet uniquely decomposes predicted adsorption energies into contributions from individual atoms within the local adsorbate graph - an interpretability feature unattainable with conventional machine-learning potentials. AdsNet thus establishes an accurate, highly efficient, and interpretable framework for large-scale adsorption energy prediction and local interface relaxation across various material surfaces.
relevance_reason: Develops an equivariant graph neural network trained on DFT structures to predict adsorption energies and forces for atomistic relaxation; (a) explicit atoms, (b) ML force/energy model, (c) method advance and application.

title: Ab-initio study of magnetic interaction in RNiO2: role of rare-earth size and epitaxial strain
abstract:
arXiv:2611.25907v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In this paper we present a systematic first-principles investigation of the structure and nearest-neighbor magnetic exchange interactions in the infinite-layer RNiO2 thin-film series (R = La-Lu), under the constrain of different substrates. Density functional theory calculations are first employed to optimize the crystal structures, while CAS+DDCI correlated wave-function calculations were used for the determination of the magnetic exchanges. This methodology allows to obtain magnetic interactions in good agreement with RIXS experimental estimations. In the pristine case, our results confirm that the structure of RNiO2 (except for R = La and Ce) adopts the I4/mcm space group, characterized by an out-of-plane rotation of the NiO4 plaquettes. This result remains valid under substrate constrains, even if compressive strain reduces the amplitude of the rotational distortion and leads to an enhancement of the magnetic exchange interaction relative to the pristine structures. The latter are found to depend sensitively on both the rare-earth ionic radius and the applied epitaxial strain. These results highlight the role of structural distortions and substrate-induced strain in tuning magnetic interactions in infinite-layer nickelates.
relevance_reason: DFT geometry optimization plus CAS+DDCI magnetic-exchange calculations on explicit RNiO2 crystal structures; satisfies (a)-(c).

title: Molecular Dynamics Simulation of the Solidification of AlCoCuFeNi High-Entropy Alloy Nanowire
abstract:
arXiv:2611.25836v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Molecular dynamics simulation of the solidification behavior of an AlCoCuFeNi high-entropy alloy nanowire was performed using an embedded atom model potential at cooling rates of 10^11, 10^12, and 10^13 K/s. Periodic boundary conditions were applied along the nanowire axis to model an effectively infinite nanowire. The crystallization process was characterized through the temperature dependence of the potential energy. Structural evolution was analyzed using adaptive common-neighbor analysis (CNA) and radial distribution functions (RDF). The results show that the final structure changes from amorphous to crystalline with decreasing cooling rate, demonstrating the strong influence of cooling conditions on phase formation in nanoscale high-entropy alloy systems.
relevance_reason: Classical molecular dynamics solidification study of an AlCoCuFeNi nanowire using an EAM potential; (a) explicit atoms, (b) classical MD, (c) applied to phase formation.

title: First-principles finite-size correction schemes for point defects of Cu$_3$N
abstract:
arXiv:2605.25153v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Point defects play a key role in determining semiconductor properties, such as electrical conductivity and photoluminescence, and often enable functional behavior. Accurate first-principles supercell simulations of point defects require reliable finite-size corrections. In this study, we combine PBE+U structural relaxations with HSE hybrid-functional calculations to determine defect formation energies and thermodynamic transition levels of Cu$_3$N. Finite-size trends are quantified using $\Gamma$-point calculations in supercells containing 256, 864, and 2048 atoms. We assess and extend the Makov-Payne and Lany-Zunger correction schemes by introducing additional $1/L^n$ terms, together with core-level potential alignment and defect-specific scaling models. Using Cu$_3$N as a case study, we show that charged vacancies are accurately described by the Makov-Payne-type scaling ($1/L + 1/L^{3}$), whereas interstitial defects with shallow or weakly localized electronic character are better captured by a hydrogenic impurity model that accounts for defect-band dispersion. Residual trends for neutral or weakly localized defects are described by higher-order polynomial fits in $1/L^{3}$ and $1/L^{4}$. Hybrid-functional energetics corrected using PBE+U-based finite-size trends confirm the intrinsic $p-n$ doping character of Cu$_3$N under the conditions considered and demonstrate that no single finite-size correction can be transferred across all defect types.
relevance_reason: DFT supercell defect calculations (PBE+U relaxations, HSE, finite-size correction scheme development) on explicit atomistic models satisfy (a)-(c) as DFT method development.

title: Strain-driven stability modulation and Mott transitions in the charge density wave phase of monolayer 1T-TaS 2
abstract: The 1T polymorph of a tantalum disulfide (1T-TaS2) monolayer exhibits a set of charge density waves (CDWs) at ambient temperature. Recent studies have found that external parameters such as strain, pressure and electric field can tune the properties of charge density waves. Although some studies on the effects of strain have been conducted, a stability analysis of the CDWs as a function of electronic correlation strength has not yet been reported, and is critical for practical applications. In this work, we initially employ first-principals calculations to calculate the electronic properties of monolayer 1T-TaS2. We thoroughly investigate how the reconstructed commensurate charge density wave (CCDW) state responds to biaxial strain when local electronic correlations are included through the Hubbard parameter U. The CCDW reconstruction already produces a finite PBE (Perdew–Burke–Ernzerhof) gap, and increasing U further strengthens the insulating state. The strain response is therefore discussed as a coupled lattice–correlation effect rather than as bandwidth modulation alone. Our results establish that 1T-TaS2 is a very promising material to be implemented in the next generation of devices, with strain providing a route to tune between correlated insulating and metallic electronic states.
relevance_reason: Uses first-principles DFT+U calculations on explicit monolayer 1T-TaS2 atomic structures to study strain effects, satisfying (a) explicit atoms, (b) DFT, and (c) application to a material system.

title: Density–orientational order coupling in isotropic melts of flexible linear polymers
abstract: We investigate the coupling between density fluctuations and chain-orientational fluctuations in isotropic melts of linear polymers. Using TraPPE United-Atom molecular dynamics simulations of polyethylene oxide (PEO) and polystyrene (PS) as representative flexible polymers, we demonstrate that this coupling, originating from microscopic chain connectivity, persists even in highly flexible systems with persistence lengths of only a few monomer units. Although density-coupled fluctuation modes are obscured by the intrachain structure factor at the system sizes accessible in simulations, we identify and quantify the density–orientation coupling by analyzing fluctuation components uncorrelated with density fluctuations. The coupling strength is substantially larger in PS than in PEO, consistent with its greater chain rigidity. Using the Fokker–Planck equation for the worm-like chain orientational probability distribution on the unit sphere, we calculate the variance of the chain’s nematic order and derive an entropic estimate of the nematic order stiffness in an isotropic system of independent semiflexible chains, which closely reproduces previously reported values for DNA solutions spanning more than two orders of magnitude in chain length. The results highlight density–orientation coupling as a universal, measurable feature of linear polymer liquids, observable even in isotropic systems of highly flexible chains and, in principle, recoverable from fluctuation trajectories of any simulated polymer melt.
relevance_reason: TraPPE united-atom classical MD simulations of PEO and PS melts analyzing density-orientational coupling, satisfying explicit atoms (a), classical MD (b), and a physical application (c).

title: Connectivity-governed mechanics of aerogels revealed through hierarchical deformation and the stretched-path framework
abstract: We numerically investigated the mechanical response of aerogels using coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations. The effect of the bond-creation probability—experimentally tunable through pH control—was examined at a fixed volume fraction. The simulated aerogels exhibited elastic behavior at small strains, followed by abrupt yielding associated with bond rupture. A clear trade-off was identified between the elastic modulus and the yield strain: when the bond-creation probability is low, the aerogel exhibits a higher modulus but a smaller yield strain. During deformation, hierarchical and nonaffine structural rearrangements were observed, whose nature depends on the bond-creation probability. These involve cooperative motions on small length scales, accompanied by large-scale transverse nonaffine displacements and stress transmission. Analysis based on the stretched and directed path provides a unified physical picture of the characteristic length scale and its role in stress transmission. These findings offer design principles for developing flexible yet mechanically robust porous materials.
relevance_reason: Coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations of aerogel mechanics under deformation, satisfying bead-based atomistic mapping (a), classical MD (b), and a materials-physics application (c).

title: Weakly coordinating anions and solvents break the conductivity-transference-solvation tradeoff
abstract:
arXiv:2611.25375v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Lithium-metal batteries promise high energy density, but common electrolytes trade ionic conductivity against the share of current carried by lithium ions and against how strongly solvent binds those ions. We show that simultaneously weakening both interactions of the lithium ion, with solvent and with anion, relaxes this trade-off. Thus, a weakly coordinating perfluorinated alkoxyaluminate salt in liquefied fluoromethane conducts 39.2 mS cm$^{-1}$ at 25 $^\circ$C while maintaining a lithium-ion transference number of 0.71. Molecular dynamics simulations further reveal that the anion prevents persistent ion aggregation and lowers the salt's dissociation penalty. Consistent with these properties, nickel-rich cathode/lithium-metal anode full cells charge at 10C at room temperature and at 2C at $-40$ $^\circ$C. We advance coordination strength as a design axis for future energy storage devices.
relevance_reason: Molecular dynamics simulations of lithium electrolyte solvation and aggregation; (a) explicit atoms, (b) classical MD, (c) applied to electrolyte design.

title: Comparative First-Principles Study of the Physical Properties, Phonon-Mediated Superconductivity and Functional Potential of Technetium-Based Binary Borides TcB2, Tc2B and Tc3B
abstract:
arXiv:2611.25554v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Phonon-mediated superconductivity in binary transition-metal borides reflects a balance between the metal d-states, metal-boron bonding, and the lattice vibrations that couple to them. Here, we compare P6/mmm TcB2 at 20 GPa with I4/mcm Tc2B and P4/mmm Tc3B at 0 GPa within a first-principles framework. Their mechanical responses differ appreciably: TcB2 is the most rigid under its compressed condition, Tc2B shows the strongest tendency toward ductility, and Tc3B falls between the two. Despite these differences, all three phases remain metallic. The states at the Fermi level are dominated by Tc-4d character, although the extent of Tc-d/B-p mixing varies from one compound to another. Charge redistribution is more directional and B-centered in TcB2, but more delocalized around the Tc network in Tc2B and Tc3B. Inclusion of spin-orbit coupling leaves all three compounds metallic. The optical response remains metallic and electric field polarization dependent, with substantial visible reflectivity and strong ultraviolet absorption. Low-frequency Tc rich vibrations dominate the electron-phonon coupling (EPC). With {\mu}* = 0.10, the Tc values of TcB2, Tc2B, and Tc3B are 24.92, 11.07, and 15.12 K, respectively. Although Tc3B exhibits a higher electronic density of states at the Fermi level, N(EF), TcB2 couples most strongly to EPC-active low-frequency modes, showing that the superconducting hierarchy depends on electronic-phonon matching rather than DOS magnitude alone.
relevance_reason: First-principles DFT calculations of explicit crystal structures including phonons and electron-phonon coupling for Tc borides satisfy (a)-(c) as a DFT application study of real atomic systems.

title: Randomized Block Davidson Eigensolvers for Plane-Wave Density-Functional Theory
abstract:
arXiv:2608.24529v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Iterative diagonalization is the dominant cost of plane-wave density-functional theory (DFT), with search-space orthogonalization scaling particularly quickly with problem size and the number of target states. We present a randomized block Davidson-type eigensolver that replaces Euclidean orthogonalization with randomized Gram-Schmidt in a sketched inner product, requiring only a single pass over the basis while keeping its conditioning bounded independently of the input vectors. This modification changes only the Rayleigh-Ritz step, which becomes a definite generalized Hermitian eigenproblem. Ritz extraction remains exact, preserving true Ritz pairs and the interlacing property that makes each band energy an upper bound on the true one. The method is implemented in mixed precision for CPUs and GPUs from a single Julia code, interfaces matrix-free with DFTK, and is released in the open-source RandESC library. On sparse test problems with a fixed number of eigenpairs, the sketched solver overtakes its deterministic counterpart beyond matrix dimensions of about $2\times 10^4$ and is $25\%$ faster at $5\times 10^5$. In full self-consistent field DFT calculations, the benefits of sketching depend on the application case. With standard pseudopotentials and plane-wave cutoffs, efficiency gains are limited. As the number of requested states grows with system size, orthogonalization savings are offset by the generalized eigenproblem. However, some highly accurate pseudopotentals require larger cutoffs, and in this regime, the randomized solver is measurably better by $6\%$ overall. Its relative efficiency also improves as simulated systems get larger.
relevance_reason: Develops a randomized block Davidson eigensolver and benchmarks it inside self-consistent plane-wave DFT (DFTK), satisfying (a) explicit atomistic basis, (b) DFT, and (c) advancing DFT methodology.

title: Efficient Spin-Orbit Coupling in Algebraic Diagrammatic Construction Theory: A State-Interaction Approach
abstract:
arXiv:2609.30772v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Spin-orbit coupling and electron correlation play important roles in a broad range of chemical and physical phenomena. In this work, we systematically assess the performance of single-reference algebraic diagrammatic construction combined with state interaction (SI-ADC) for describing electronic structure in the presence of spin-orbit coupling. We find that second-order SI-ADC methods (SI-ADC(2)) achieve zero-field-splitting accuracies comparable to those of higher-level and more computationally demanding approaches, including variational four-component ADC and two-component ADC methods based on spin-orbit effective Hamiltonians. We further demonstrate the broad applicability of SI-ADC by evaluating a diverse range of spin-orbit-coupled properties, including electron affinities, ionization potentials, neutral excitation energies, core-ionization energies, and magnetic g-tensors, for systems ranging from small molecules to transition-metal complexes and f-block compounds. Across these applications, SI-ADC(2) methods provide consistently accurate results, likely benefiting in part from favorable error cancellation between electron-correlation and spin-orbit effects. In contrast, SI-ADC(3) methods are generally less accurate, particularly for systems containing transition-metal and heavy elements. Overall, these results establish SI-ADC as an efficient and broadly applicable framework for incorporating spin-orbit coupling into ADC calculations of electronic and spectroscopic properties.
relevance_reason: Development and benchmarking of spin-orbit-coupled SI-ADC (a post-Hartree-Fock propagator/electronic-structure method) for zero-field splittings, g-tensors, and ionization/excitation energies of explicit molecular systems: (a) and (b) hold via post-HF method development, and (c) holds as a methodological advance, though it is electronic-structure theory rather than dynamics.

title: A plane-wave auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo study of silicon point defects
abstract:
arXiv:2611.25121v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Accurately predicting the energetics of point defects remains a formidable challenge in computational materials science. For the tetrahedral silicon self-interstitial, for example, previous periodic coupled-cluster [CCSD(T)] and diffusion Monte Carlo (DMC) calculations disagree by about 1.2 eV. Here, we present formation energies of silicon self-interstitials and vacancies using auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo (AFQMC) in a plane-wave basis formulated within the projector-augmented wave framework, and compare them with the random-phase approximation (RPA) and CCSD(T). Using 16- and 64-atom cells, we demonstrate that an RPA-based correction effectively removes the two-body finite-size errors that remain after twist averaging in AFQMC for bulk silicon and for the dumbbell and hexagonal self-interstitials. With this correction, we obtain formation energies of 4.4 eV and 4.6 eV for these two self-interstitials in 16-atom cells, in good agreement with DMC and transcorrelated coupled-cluster results. For the tetrahedral interstitial and the Jahn--Teller-distorted vacancy, 16-atom cells are too small to obtain realistic formation energies; in 64-atom cells, we obtain 5.7 eV and 5.2 eV, respectively. With identical setups in 16-atom cells, CCSD(T) yields systematically lower formation energies than AFQMC, with the largest difference, 250 meV, for the tetrahedral interstitial. Our results indicate that the earlier overestimation of CCSD(T) for the tetrahedral interstitial stems from the finite-size treatment in the coupled-cluster workflow rather than from multi-configurational character of the defect.
relevance_reason: Plane-wave auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo (with PAW formulation and RPA finite-size corrections) computes silicon self-interstitial and vacancy formation energies on explicit periodic atomistic cells, compared against CCSD(T) and DMC: (a) and (b) are satisfied by a correlated many-body electronic-structure method, and (c) is satisfied by a methodological advance plus a concrete defect-energetics result.

title: First-principles carrier mobility and optical absorption of strained ZnO with self-consistent Hubbard interactions
abstract:
arXiv:2607.29030v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Carrier mobility and optical absorption are key performance parameters of oxide semiconductors in transparent and flexible displays. We use a newly developed density-functional perturbation theory with a self-consistent Hubbard correction (DFPT+U) to study phonon-limited electron transport and phonon-assisted optical absorption in strained zinc oxide (ZnO). This parameter-free approach accounts for electron-phonon interactions and on-site correlation effects simultaneously. Electronic structures and phonon dispersions are computed under three distinct uniaxial strain directions. Uniaxial tensile strain up to 4.8% along [\bar110] is found to increase the room-temperature electron mobility by 19% while leaving visible-range optical absorption essentially unchanged. These results demonstrate that moderate strain can selectively enhance carrier transport without degrading optical transparency, and establish DFPT+U as an effective framework for predicting strain-dependent transport and optical properties in wide-band-gap oxides with implications for strain-engineered display and optoelectronic applications.
relevance_reason: DFPT+U development and application to phonon-limited transport and optical absorption in strained ZnO is a DFT method/application study on explicit atomic structures, satisfying (a)-(c).
